# Results — Study 635 (Coinbase Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**when US institutions buy, Coinbase trades rich to Binance, and the premium leads the
market** (the "Coinbase Premium Gap" popularised by CryptoQuant in the 2020-21 bull) —
rebuilt from the two venues' own public APIs: Coinbase Exchange BTC-USD daily candles vs
Binance BTCUSDT daily klines, both stamped on the same 00:00-UTC boundary. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete UTC day; June 2026 is the last complete month).
Fingerprint `73bf2b138404`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | **Coinbase Exchange** `/products/BTC-USD/candles` (UTC daily, USD leg) + **Binance** `/api/v3/klines` BTCUSDT 1d (USDT leg) — both public, keyless |
| Window | **3,240 joint days**, 2017-08-17 (Binance listing) → 2026-06-30 (**8.9 years**) |
| Premium | `cb/bn − 1` in bps at the shared UTC close — the industry's standard construction |
| Signal | premium **level** (and 1-day change) at close *t*; overlay uses the trailing **63-day z-score**, past-only |
| Execution / costs | **exactly one execution lag**: signal read at close *t*, position earns the close-*t* → close-*t+1* Coinbase USD return; costs **one-way bps × traded NAV** per position change; long-only, no borrow; rf = 0 on both Sharpe legs (labeled) |

> **Named caveat — the USDT leg.** The Binance side is quoted in **USDT**, so the
> "premium" mixes the true Coinbase USD bid with the USDT/USD peg: a Tether stress day
> moves the series with no Coinbase flow at all (the ±200-500 bps prints of 2017-18 are
> largely peg noise). We name it and carry a **1%/99% winsorized** robustness leg rather
> than pretend the two are separable at daily resolution. No survivorship: one asset,
> two venues, both alive the whole window.

## The premium series — the regime narrative

Mean **+1.54 bps**, sd **64.0 bps**, range **−535 → +1,335 bps**, AC(1) **0.71**
(persistent). Contemporaneously the premium co-moves with same-day returns (corr
**+0.077**, HAC *t* = +1.91) — it is at least a coincident tell of the US bid.

| year | mean (bps) | sd | share > 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2017 | **+107.37** | 198.66 | 76% |
| 2018 | −33.84 | 110.90 | 42% |
| 2019 | −4.45 | 57.85 | 54% |
| 2020 | **+5.95** | 14.16 | 72% |
| 2021 | **+5.94** | 6.71 | **88%** |
| 2022 | −1.08 | 7.04 | 61% |
| 2023 | +3.19 | 9.60 | 75% |
| 2024 | −0.02 | 6.82 | 52% |
| 2025 | +0.43 | 4.78 | 60% |
| 2026 (H1) | **−5.62** | 6.28 | **20%** |

The folklore's shape is on the tape: 2020-21 — the Saylor/Tesla institutional-bid era —
is the one stretch where Coinbase sat *persistently* rich (positive on 72-88% of days),
and the premium's scale collapsed ~10-20× once cross-venue arbitrage matured. 2026 H1
is the mirror image: Coinbase **cheap on 145/181 days** (mean −5.6 bps).

## Predictive regressions — does the premium *lead* the market?

Forward *h*-day Coinbase log return on today's premium; **HAC (Newey-West) *t*** on the
slope, lags = *h* + 2. Beta per +1 sd of the signal.

| h | LEVEL raw — beta (bps/sd) | HAC *t* | LEVEL winsorized — beta | HAC *t* | Δ1d — HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1d | +12.47 | **+1.42** | +20.81 | **+2.30** | +0.22 |
| 2d | +23.08 | +1.76 | +32.98 | **+2.22** | −0.26 |
| 3d | +37.97 | **+2.09** | +46.99 | **+2.10** | −0.17 |
| 5d | +53.36 | +1.48 | +68.38 | +1.71 | +1.12 |
| 7d | +61.37 | +1.16 | +90.72 | +1.63 | +0.62 |

The direction is positive at **every** horizon, but the claim's headline spec — raw
level → next-day return — sits at **HAC *t* = +1.42**, below the desk's bar. Winsorizing
the USDT-depeg tails (bounds −215.8/+178.7 bps) lifts h = 1-3 to **2.10-2.30**, and raw
h = 3 touches **2.09** — the whisper firms exactly when you clean the peg noise, but the
legs that clear 2 depend on that spec choice. The 1-day **change** predicts nothing
(all |*t*| ≤ 1.12). The group split says the same: next-day return is **+17.77 bps** on
rich days (z63 > 0) vs **+0.18 bps** on cheap days — a fat-looking gap at only Welch
*t* = **+1.40** against crypto's daily noise.

## Tradability — the timing overlay cannot certify itself

Long BTC for day *t+1* iff z63(premium) > 0 at close *t* (47.3% exposure, 76 position
changes/yr), vs buy & hold **+8.07 bps/d** (Sharpe 0.43, ann +34.3%).

| one-way cost | net bps/d | HAC *t* | Sharpe | net ann | timing alpha bps/d (HAC *t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | +7.38 | +1.67 | 0.56 | +30.9% | +3.55 (**+1.13**) |
| 10 bps | +6.34 | +1.43 | 0.48 | +26.1% | +2.52 (**+0.80**) |
| 25 bps | +3.24 | +0.73 | 0.24 | +12.6% | −0.58 (**−0.18**) |

Timing alpha = net overlay − exposure-matched buy & hold, the honest "is the *timing*
worth anything" series. It never clears 1.2 at realistic costs and is negative at 25 bps.
Window robustness (10 bps): z20 alpha *t* = +2.15, z63 = +0.80, z126 = +1.48 — the one
window that clears the bar is a **spec-search artefact**, not a headline. The
exposure-matched **random-timing twin (20 seeds)** earns −1.46 ± 2.98 bps/d (mean HAC
*t* = −0.33): the machinery pays nothing for luck.

## Eras + third axis — did the ETF era kill the signal?

| era | n | prem mean (sd) bps | pred beta bps/sd | HAC *t* | overlay alpha bps/d (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2017-2019 | 867 | +0.85 (122.83) | +19.89 | +1.21 | +6.02 (+0.86) |
| 2020-2021 (institutional bid) | 731 | +5.95 (11.08) | +10.43 | +0.56 | −6.04 (−0.79) |
| 2022 | 365 | −1.08 (7.04) | +4.95 | +0.29 | +7.14 (+0.69) |
| **2023+** | 1,277 | +0.23 (7.68) | **+29.15** | **+2.87** | +1.23 (+0.34) |
| 2024+ (ETF era proper) | 912 | −0.95 (6.40) | +16.90 | +1.80 | +4.24 (+0.97) |

The pre-registered myth-check — *post-2022, with the institutional bid clearing through
ETFs elsewhere, the premium signal should be dead* — is **busted**. The premium's
*level* compressed ~10-20× and 2026 sits persistently negative, but per bp of premium
the predictive slope is **22× larger** in 2023+ than before (+3.793 vs +0.175 bps of
next-day return per bp; HAC-SE difference *t* = **+2.72**), and 2023+ is the **only**
era whose raw h = 1 *t* clears 2 (+2.87). A compressed premium that says *more* per bp
— consistent with a maturing arb where any residual gap is genuine net flow. (Amusingly,
2020-21 itself — the era the folklore celebrates — predicts nothing: *t* = +0.56. The
premium was rich then, but *knowing* it was rich earned you nothing extra.) The 2024+
slice alone is *t* = +1.80: the sharpened signal is thin enough that the ETF-era
sub-sample cannot re-certify it on its own.

## Synthetic control — the engine is faithful *(machinery proof only, never evidence)*

Two-venue world, AR(1) premium around a shared random walk, planted "premium leads
returns" knob:

| planted lead | h=1 beta (bps/sd) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 (null) | +4.75 | +0.75 |
| 0.003 | +34.05 | **+5.35** |

The detector stays quiet on a pure-noise premium and lights up on a planted lead — the
real-tape *t*'s are read off an honest instrument.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The premium leans the right way at every horizon and in every era,
  and it is a real coincident tell (corr +0.077 with same-day returns) — but the claim
  as stated (level → next-day return) is **HAC *t* = +1.42** on 8.9 years of tape.
  The legs that clear 2 (winsorized h = 1-3 at 2.10-2.30, raw h = 3 at 2.09, 2023+ at
  2.87) all require a spec or sample choice. The tape shows a whisper, not a certified
  signal; the 2020-21 "institutional bid" era itself predicts nothing (*t* = +0.56).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long-only timing overlay's alpha over exposure-matched
  buy & hold is **+0.80 HAC *t*** at 10 bps one-way, negative at 25 bps, and
  window-fragile (z20 = +2.15 vs z63 = +0.80 vs z126 = +1.48 — spec search, not edge).
  A 20-seed random twin confirms the machinery pays nothing for luck. Costs and spec
  sensitivity eat the whisper entirely.
- **"Dead since the ETFs?" — BUSTED.** The premium compressed ~10-20× and 2026 H1 is
  80% *negative* — but per bp it now says **22× more** (slope difference *t* = +2.72),
  and 2023+ is the only slice that clears the bar on its own (*t* = +2.87). The signal
  did not die with the ETFs; it shrank and sharpened.
